title: Raspberry-Apple Pie
ingredients:
Pie Crust:
2 ½ cups all-purpose flour
1 tablespoon granulated sugar
1 teaspoon salt
1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
6–8 tablespoons ice water

Pie Filling:
4–5 cups apples (about 4–5 medium apples: Granny Smith or Honeycrisp), peeled, cored, and sliced very thin (about 1/8-inch thick)
2 cups fresh raspberries
¾ cup granulated sugar
¼ cup light brown sugar, packed
¼ cup cornstarch
1 tablespoon lemon juice
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
¼ teaspoon ground nutmeg
1 tablespoon butter, cubed (to dot the top)

For top finishing:
1 egg white, lightly beaten (to waterproof the bottom crust)
1 whole egg + 1 tablespoon milk (for the top crust egg wash)
1 tablespoon coarse baking sugar (optional, for crunch)
instructions:
Make the Crust: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, granulated sugar, and salt. Add the cold, cubed butter and use a pastry cutter or your fingers to work the butter in until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces remaining.

Hydrate and Chill the Dough: Drizzle 6 tablespoons of ice water over the mixture. Stir gently with a spatula. Add up to 2 more tablespoons of water if the dough is too dry to hold together when pinched. Divide into two discs, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Prepare the Bottom Crust: On a lightly floured surface, roll one dough disc into a 12-inch circle. Carefully drape it into a 9-inch pie dish. Brush the bottom and lower sides of the crust with a thin layer of the lightly beaten egg white (this prevents a soggy bottom). Place the dish in the fridge while you prepare the fruit.

Mix the Filling: In a large bowl, combine the thinly sliced apples, fresh raspberries, granulated sugar, brown sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Toss gently. The raspberries will begin to break down as you mix—this is intended and will create a jam-like sauce around the thin apples.

Assemble the Pie: Pour the fruit filling into the chilled bottom crust, mounding it slightly in the center. Dot the top of the fruit evenly with the cubed tablespoon of butter.

Top the Pie: Roll out the second dough disc. Cover the pie with a solid top crust (cutting at least 4 slits for steam to escape) or weave a lattice pattern. Trim the overhang, fold the edges under, and crimp to seal.

Final Chill: Place the fully assembled pie into the refrigerator for 20 to 30 minutes. Meanwhile, preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C) and place an empty baking sheet on the lowest rack to heat up.

Egg Wash and Bake: Brush the top crust with the egg-and-milk wash and sprinkle evenly with coarse sugar. Place the pie onto the preheated baking sheet in the oven. Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes.

Reduce Heat and Finish: Lower the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and bake for an additional 35–45 minutes. If the crust edges are browning too quickly, tent them with an aluminum foil ring. The pie is done when the crust is deep golden brown and the filling juices are bubbling thickly through the center vents.

Cool: Transfer the pie to a wire rack. Let it cool completely for at least 3 to 4 hours before slicing so the juices can set.
